slides.text: Beyond the edge of every charted archipelago lies the Mare Vitreum—the Glass Sea—where the wind died seven centuries ago and water crystallized into luminous, motionless sapphire. No tide ebbs; no fish swims. Time there is not a river but an amber block. Navigators enter only on ice-skiffs equipped with bone runners, gliding silently between the frozen hulls of hundred-gun galleons and imperial triremes trapped mid-tempest with their billowing sails stiff as carved alabaster.

For forty leagues, navigator Kael skimmed across the mirror glaze, scouting for salvage among the preserved centuries. He passed an admiral standing on a poop deck, sword raised toward a thunderhead that had not moved since the reign of the Sun King. He saw cannonballs hanging suspended in the crisp air between two rival frigates, halos of silver frost clinging to their iron curves. Nothing breathed. Nothing decayed. It was a cathedral of unfinished moments.

Then, near the center of the stillness, Kael found a humble rowboat adrift on the blue glass. Inside sat an archer and a weaver girl in moth-eaten linen, their foreheads pressed together, hands intertwined over a small crust of bread. As Kael’s skiff carved past them, the weaver girl’s eyelid gave a microscopic flutter, and a single crystalline tear detached from her cheek, taking three weeks to fall into her lap. Love was the only thing the ice couldn't stop.
